target_customer: Data center, AI cluster and optical communication builders needing chip-scale multi-wavelength laser sources; also government and research programs
problem: Moving data between processors and racks with copper limits bandwidth and energy efficiency; multicolor comb lasers can replace dozens of discrete lasers with one chip.
business_model: Hardware and component sales, research contracts and grants; pilot production planned for 2027
product_category: Photonics hardware, integrated multicolor comb lasers for optical interconnects

founders.name: John Jost
founders.background_notes: YC page: 20+ years in quantum, atomic and optical physics, 70+ publications, worked with two Nobel winning physicists; employers and education not named.

founders.name: Maxim Karpov
founders.background_notes: EPFL and CSEM from Horizons magazine via search result; YC page lists PhD and 40+ papers. Named MIT Innovator Under 35 in 2025 per optics.org.

competitors.name: Ayar Labs
competitors.what: In-package optical I/O chiplets using light to move data between chips
competitors.traction_then: Commercializing optical I/O products per the funding release
competitors.funding_then: $130M Series C announced April 2022 (about three months after the batch start)

technical_complexity.rationale: Research-grade integrated photonics: chip-scale microcomb lasers that must be mass manufacturable, with spin-off roots in academic comb research.

defensibility.rationale: Deep physics expertise and long development cycles raise barriers; no patent count verified.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; large players invest in optical interconnect in general per optics.org.

market_need_then: AI and data center bandwidth and power demand were growing in 2022 and drove funding of optical interconnect startups such as Ayar Labs.

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests light and is distinctive, but no brand coverage or community found; trademark filed in the US in May 2024.

outcome_analysis: Enlightra is an EPFL linked photonics spin-off in YC W22 building chip-scale multicolor comb lasers for AI interconnects. It lived on non-dilutive funding and research programs for years, then announced $15M in December 2025 from YC, Runa Capital and others. It is a long cycle hardware company with pilot production planned for 2027, so success is not yet proven.
notes: The $15M figure is stated by optics.org and The Quantum Insider; stage not stated by the source so recorded as other. Seedtable calls it pre-seed (estimate); Caplight lists $2.62M, conflicting and not used. Founding year conflicts: 2018 (CB Insights), 2021 and November 2021 (Horizons, startup.ch), 2022 (optics.org). YC page says 2021. Non-dilutive funding of over $2M is claimed on the YC page, not itemized. Earlier rounds not found. Ayar Labs source is about three months after the batch start; no pre-batch competitor opened. Karpov's EPFL and CSEM roles come from a search summary of Horizons magazine, not opened.
